title: Fix 'Permission denied' when running a script
summary: Running a script gives Permission denied when the file is not marked as runnable. You can check the file's permissions and add the run permission to fix it.

aliases.text: how to make a script executable
не запускается скрипт sh отказано в доступе
ошибка permission denied при запуске скрипта
как дать права на запуск скрипта

prerequisites: You have a script file in a folder you can open in Terminal
You own the script file or can change its permissions

steps.explain: Look at the file's permissions. The first column shows the rights: r means read, w means write, x means run. If there is no x in the first group of characters, the system refuses to run the file.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: File name of the script in the current folder.

steps.expect: A line like -rw-r--r-- ... myscript.sh. No x in the first 10 characters means the file is not executable.

steps.explain: Add the run permission for everyone. This changes only the file's permission bits, not its contents.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: File name of the script in the current folder.

alternatives.explain: Add the run permission only for your own user account, not for other users.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: File name of the script in the current folder.

steps.explain: Run the script. It should start now, without the Permission denied message.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: File name of the script in the current folder, without the ./ part.

steps.expect: The script's own output appears and there is no Permission denied line.

alternatives.explain: Run the script through bash without changing its permissions. Bash reads the file itself, so the run permission is not needed.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: File name of the script in the current folder.

verify.expect: The first group of characters now contains x, for example -rwxr-xr-x.

warnings: Make a script executable only if you trust where it came from. A script runs with your permissions and can change files on your computer.
On a USB stick or network drive mounted with the noexec option, chmod does not help. Use the bash alternative in the last step.
